last.verdict: Moderna swung to a profit on international COVID vaccine sales and raised its revenue outlook, but the cash jump comes mostly from borrowing.

takeaways.label: Profit and higher outlook
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 29% to $1.3B, with net income of $162M versus a $200M loss a year earlier. Full-year growth is now guided to 15–25%, up from up to 10%.

takeaways.label: Cash boosted by debt
takeaways.text: Year-end cash is now forecast at $8.1–8.3B, up from $4.7–5.2B. The quarter included $2.6B net from convertible notes, and $1.4B of receivables were still uncollected.

takeaways.label: Melanoma shot is the big upside
takeaways.text: Phase 3 data showed the cancer vaccine intismeran plus Keytruda cut recurrence or death risk 42% versus Keytruda alone. Regulatory filings with Merck are being prepared.

takeaways.label: Costs lower, flu launch limited
takeaways.text: 2026 R&D spending is now about $2.7B, down from $2.9B. The newly approved flu shot launches only in limited form this season. The norovirus vaccine has no clear path.

history.verdict: Norovirus vaccine setback outweighed a smaller-than-expected loss and lower costs.

reasons.label: Norovirus vaccine setback
reasons.text: Phase 3 norovirus vaccine missed early-success bar; more patients must be enrolled, delaying it.

reasons.label: Pipeline over numbers
reasons.text: Revenue is only $145M, so the stock trades on upcoming flu and melanoma news.

reasons.label: Cost cuts, cash runway
reasons.text: Spending outlook trimmed about $0.2B; year-end cash now seen at $4.7–5.2B.
